paragraphs: The 316d was part of the F30/F31 3 Series generation from 2012 to 2019. Early cars (2012–2015) use the N47 — a 1.5-litre diesel from the older engine family, with a well-documented timing chain guide wear issue that's been the subject of recalls. From 2015, the facelift LCI generation switched to the B47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's genuinely different under the bonnet and significantly more reliable. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 316d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.5-litre diesel fitted to the 316d from 2012 to 2015. Known for timing chain guide wear and failure over time — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides and tensioners as standard on every N47 rebuild.
A 2.0-litre diesel fitted from 2015. A genuinely different, more reliable design from the N47 with no equivalent to the older engine's well-documented timing chain pattern.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW 3 Series 316d can use the N47 or B47 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47 or B47) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 316d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
